description.narrative: The OECD, UN Environment and the World Bank Group have joined forces under a new initiative Financing Climate Futures: Rethinking Infrastructure. The initiative explored what public and private actors should do to trigger the radical transformation needed to align financial flows in infrastructure for a low-emission, resilient development. The initiative, supported by the German Federal Ministry of the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMU), stems from the 2017 G20 Hamburg Climate and Energy Action Plan, which called on the three organisations to “compile ongoing public and private activities within the G20 for making financial flows consistent with the Paris goals and, building on this, to analyse potential opportunities for strengthening these efforts”.
